CHIEF COMPLAINT
Yearly exam.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Beverly is a 24-year-old female with a history of type 2 diabetes and hypertension presenting for her yearly physical examination. She reports feeling well overall. She recently began working at a bakery this summer, which she is enjoying. However, due to her proximity to desserts and treats at work, she has been snacking frequently and consuming significantly more sweets than usual. She notes that her blood sugars have been up and down, which she attributes to her diet. She reports taking her diabetes medication as prescribed without any missed doses. Her blood pressure has been good despite the fluctuations in blood sugar. She is sleeping well, getting a full eight hours of sleep nightly. She denies any suicidal or self-harm ideation.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Reviewed by nurse and patient. No additional concerns reported beyond those discussed in history of present illness.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Type 2 diabetes mellitus
Hypertension
Grade 2 systolic ejection murmur (unchanged)

MEDICATIONS
Metformin twice daily
Lisinopril 10 mg once daily

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Recently employed at a bakery as of summer 2026. Reports difficulty resisting temptation from desserts and treats at workplace.

General: Normal exam
Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; grade 2 systolic ejection murmur appreciated, unchanged from prior
Pulmonary: Lungs clear bilaterally
Neurological: Grips equal bilaterally; neurovascular exam intact
Extremities: No edema; pulses good

Strength: Intact bilaterally

RESULTS
Hemoglobin A1C: Elevated
Blood glucose: Elevated

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus - poorly controlled
   - Patient's hyperglycemia appears diet-related due to increased snacking and dessert consumption at new job
   - Goal hemoglobin A1C <7%, preferably <6%
   - No medication changes at this time
   - Patient to cut down on snacking and additional sweets
   - Patient to check fasting blood sugars in morning and call in results in 2 weeks
   - Follow-up visit in 2 months to reassess control
   - If no improvement noted, will consider adding additional antidiabetic medication

2. Hypertension - stable
   - Continue lisinopril 10 mg once daily
   - No changes to current regimen
   - Blood pressure well-controlled on current therapy
